A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same M2A masking-family study. All 28 pages of v2 and 35 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original M2A classification, aquaculture recognition, segmentation, and adaptation-ablation results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds mask-sampling, selection-strategy, and adaptation-setting experiments.

M1.justification: v3 adds experimental M2A variants with checkerboard sampling, center/local-entropy mask selection, and recovery/filtering components. The main losses and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The Block-Patch clarification alone does not establish that the implementation underlying the retained main results changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10-C, CIFAR-100-C, ImageNet-C, MRSFFIA-C, and CarlaTTA, retaining the classification, feeding-intensity recognition, and segmentation tasks. The added experiments vary masking and adaptation procedures within existing coverage.

E2.justification: SPA, previously discussed without reported comparison scores, is added to all three Table 1 benchmark panels. Figure 21 also compares Random selection with Center and local-histogram Uncertainty selection within M2A. Existing external comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds controlled selection-rule comparisons holding family, loss, and pipeline fixed, and crosses masking families with recovery/filtering, CL+EL versus CL+RL, and one to three updates per batch. Table 8 compares mask geometries under three masking schedules. These substantially expand the experimental design; retained benchmark protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether contiguity explains patch stability (Table 8), whether family rankings survive alternative training procedures (Figures 15–17), and whether selection heuristics help within a fixed family (Figure 21). Existing loss, hyperparameter, small-batch, architecture, and reordered-stream analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seeds 1, 2, and 3 and retain the same mean/standard-deviation reporting practice. No increased run count, new confidence intervals, significance testing, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Retained table values and figure results are unchanged. v3 adds SPA mean errors of 23.5%, 29.0%, and 39.8% in Table 1. New Table 8 reports 37.39% for Block-Patch versus 51.00% for Free-Patch and 51.37% for Grid-Patch at the 0–10–20% schedule. Further results cover modified training and selection procedures; these are added comparisons, not improvements to retained scores.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.3 introduces mathematical definitions for retained energy, boundary-based coherence, spectral-damage overlap, and a structural-preservation index with threshold conditions. This substantially expands the formal account beyond v2's verbal principle. The quantities are explicitly unestimated and the conditions heuristic, without proofs or guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract and two principal empirical contributions remain. The introduction and conclusion narrow the mechanistic claim from a predictive principle to a conceptual explanation, make selection-strategy refinement tentative, and explicitly leave generalization beyond the tested M2A framework unverified.

C2.justification: v3 substantially qualifies the central mechanism interpretation. Section 4.7 gives the existing information-removal asymmetry caveat explicit implications for causal isolation, while Appendix A.3 states that structural preservation is neither a calibrated predictor nor an established sole mechanism. New discussions interpret the geometry, update-rule, and selection controls.

D1.justification: The patch-sampling specification is revised from v2's multiple-patch/rejection-sampling description to an explicit contiguous token-grid block construction. New variants receive implementation formulas, including grayscale conversion, 16 intensity bins, and 9×9 local histograms for Uncertainty selection. Core optimization and dataset-preparation details remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds Hondru et al.'s masked-image-modeling survey to delimit input zero-out masking, and Niu et al. (2022), EATA, to motivate recovery/filtering experiments. The existing related-work section and positioning against masking-based CTTA methods are largely retained.

P1.justification: v3 edits methodology and interpretation passages, rewrites the conclusion, adds main-text limitations and acknowledgements, and expands the appendix organization and discussion. It introduces Block-Patch terminology and changes author order. Much of the existing prose and section sequence remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the comparative displays with the mask-sampling Table 8 and multi-panel Figures 15–17 and 21. Table 1 gains SPA rows. Existing figures are retained, with relocations and appendix renumbering; for example, v2 Figures 15–17 become v3 Figures 18–20.

improvement.justification: The added geometry, training-procedure, and within-M2A selection controls strengthen support for the retained findings. Sections 4.7, 5, and A.3 also better distinguish empirical observations from an unvalidated mechanism. These improve an already extensive study, but the new preservation index remains untested and stronger causal wording persists elsewhere, including Section 4.5.
